title: Demonstration 3: Multiomics (scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq) Simulation Evaluation
text: Single-cell multiomics technologies allow simultaneous parallel measurement multiple cellular features — commonly gene expression (scRNA-seq) chromatin accessibility (scATAC-seq). Simulating multiomics data presents unique challenges algorithms must preserve distinct statistical properties individual modality, also biological coupling regulatory relationships . scSimEval designed evaluate simulation fidelity across two primary multiomics experimental designs, tailored level cell-level pairing modalities: Paired Multiomics (co-assay profiling identical individual cells) Unpaired Multiomics (independent profiling separate cells biological system). Understanding design simulated data belongs essential selecting correct evaluation functions.

title: Demonstration 3: Multiomics (scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq) Simulation Evaluation
text: Definition: scRNA-seq scATAC-seq measured simultaneously exact individual cells. cell barcode RNA matrix corresponding biologically meaningful entry column index ATAC matrix. Technologies: 10x Chromium Multiome, SHARE-seq, SNARE-seq, Paired-seq, ASTAR-seq Simulators: scMultiSim (Li et al., Nat Methods 2023), SymSim2+ATAC, MultiSim scSimEval can evaluate: ✅ Full unimodal evaluation modality (Categories 1–5, 7, 8) batch_asw (Batch Average Silhouette Width joint embedding space) cell_type_asw (Cell-Type Average Silhouette Width joint embedding space) graph_connectivity (Within-cell-type k-NN graph connectivity) ari (Adjusted Rand Index joint latent clustering) nmi (Normalized Mutual Information joint latent clustering)

title: Demonstration 3: Multiomics (scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq) Simulation Evaluation
text: Definition: scRNA-seq scATAC-seq profiled different cells derived biological tissue, cell line, sample. Cell barcodes correspond modalities — column RNA matrix column ATAC matrix represent entirely different cells. Technologies: Bulk ATAC + scRNA-seq, independent 10x scATAC + scRNA experiments tissue, sci-ATAC-seq paired scRNA-seq sibling aliquots Simulators: scDesign3, scMultiSim, scCross scSimEval can evaluate: ✅ Full unimodal evaluation modality independently (Categories 1–5, 7, 8) ✅ Joint-embedding multiomics integration metrics (Category 6) pre-integrated embeddings (integrated pca) supplied combined multiomics object via pairing = "unpaired" evaluate_multiomics_accuracy().

title: Demonstration 3: Multiomics (scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq) Simulation Evaluation
text: scSimEval includes paired scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq dataset (example_multiomics) every column RNA matrix corresponds cell ATAC matrix: dataset contains: ref_multi: Named list rna (count matrix) atac (peak accessibility matrix), measured cells. sim_multi: Simulated paired rna atac matrices. cell_types: Cell type annotations shared across modalities. batch_info: Batch labels shared across modalities. resource_stats: Hardware logs (runtime seconds peak RAM MiB).

library(scSimEval)  # Load packaged paired multiomics example dataset data(example_multiomics)  cat("Reference RNA dimensions:", dim(example_multiomics$ref_multi$rna), "

title: Demonstration 3: Multiomics (scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq) Simulation Evaluation
code: library(scSimEval) data(example_scrna)   # RNA modality data(example_scatac)  # ATAC modality (different cells)  # ── Step 1: Evaluate each modality independently ────────────────────────────── rna_eval <- evaluate_simulation_accuracy(   ref_data = example_scrna$ref,   sim_data = example_scrna$sim,   compute_bivariate = FALSE,   verbose = FALSE )  atac_eval <- evaluate_simulation_accuracy(   ref_data = example_scatac$ref,   sim_data = example_scatac$sim,   compute_bivariate = FALSE,   verbose = FALSE )  # ── Step 2: Consolidate and compare across modalities ───────────────────────── dataset_collection <- list(   "Method_A-RNA"  = list(ref = example_scrna$ref,  sim = example_scrna$sim),   "Method_A-ATAC" = list(ref = example_scatac$ref, sim = example_scatac$sim) )  consolidated <- evaluate_multiple_datasets(   datasets          = dataset_collection,   pair_by_prefix    = TRUE,   compute_bivariate = FALSE,   verbose           = FALSE )  print(consolidated$dataset_overview)

title: Demonstration 4: Analyzing Pre-Saved Benchmark Results (.rds)
text: large-scale benchmarking studies involving multiple simulation methods, diverse biological datasets, multi-core high-performance computing (HPC) clusters, running full 56 curated evaluation metric suite can take considerable time. evaluation complete, researchers typically serialize output using saveRDS() long-term storage, publication sharing, reproducible downstream analysis. scSimEval architected allow instant reloading, re-analysis, leaderboard ranking, publication-grade visualization pre-saved .rds benchmark file — without re-computing single metric. tutorial demonstrates load, inspect, rank, visualize pre-saved benchmark results R console sessions prepare interactive exploration.

title: Demonstration 4: Analyzing Pre-Saved Benchmark Results (.rds)
text: scSimEval bundles pre-computed multi-dataset benchmark archive package directory. can load directly via base R’s readRDS(): loaded object contains: * benchmark_df: complete tidy evaluations table across simulators metrics. * benchmark_summary_table: Formatted scores ready reporting. * methods: Character vector evaluated simulators (e.g., scDesign3, SCRIP, dyngen, Splatter, SymSim, simATAC). * datasets: Evaluated datasets (e.g., Rice Bud (Paired), Soybean Root (Unpaired)).
code: library(scSimEval)  # Locate the bundled benchmark file or supply your own path rds_path <- system.file("shiny", "scSimEvalApp", "data", "demo_multidataset_benchmark.rds", package = "scSimEval") if (rds_path == "") {   rds_path <- file.path("..", "inst", "shiny", "scSimEvalApp", "data", "demo_multidataset_benchmark.rds") }  # Ingest the serialized benchmark object bench_data <- readRDS(rds_path)  # Verify class and contents class(bench_data) #> [1] "scSimEval_multidataset_benchmark" "scSimEval_consolidated"           #> [3] "list" names(bench_data) #>  [1] "benchmark_df"             "granular_benchmark_table" #>  [3] "benchmark_summary_table"  "cross_dataset_stats"      #>  [5] "dataset_summary"          "dataset_summary_df"       #>  [7] "methods"                  "datasets"                 #>  [9] "is_multidataset"          "n_datasets"               #> [11] "n_simulators"

title: Demonstration 4: Analyzing Pre-Saved Benchmark Results (.rds)
text: core every scSimEval benchmark object tidy data frame following standard tidyverse conventions: row records: * Dataset: Experimental source condition. * Method: Simulation algorithm evaluated. * Category: One 8 canonical evaluation categories (e.g., () Distributional Properties, (V) Biological Signal & Differential Fidelity). * Metric: Name curated evaluation metric. * Score_Raw: Unnormalized empirical value physical units (seconds, peak RAM MiB, correlation coefficient, Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance). * Score: Standardized direction-aware fidelity score normalized [0,1][0, 1], 1.01.0 represents top fidelity.
code: # Preview top rows of the benchmark scores head(bench_data$benchmark_df[, c("Dataset", "Method", "Category", "Metric", "Score_Raw", "Score")], 8) #>             Dataset     Method                      Category      Metric #> 1 Rice Bud (Paired)  scDesign3 (I) Distributional Properties Wasserstein #> 2 Rice Bud (Paired) scMultiSim (I) Distributional Properties Wasserstein #> 3 Rice Bud (Paired)    scMoMtF (I) Distributional Properties Wasserstein #> 4 Rice Bud (Paired)    Matilda (I) Distributional Properties Wasserstein #> 5 Rice Bud (Paired)      MOSim (I) Distributional Properties Wasserstein #> 6 Rice Bud (Paired)    scCross (I) Distributional Properties Wasserstein #> 7 Rice Bud (Paired)  scDesign3 (I) Distributional Properties          KS #> 8 Rice Bud (Paired) scMultiSim (I) Distributional Properties          KS #>   Score_Raw  Score #> 1    0.0842 1.0000 #> 2    0.1014 0.8289 #> 3    0.1411 0.4334 #> 4    0.1593 0.2522 #> 5    0.1847 0.0500 #> 6    0.1299 0.5452 #> 7    0.0541 1.0000 #> 8    0.0818 0.7539

title: Demonstration 4: Analyzing Pre-Saved Benchmark Results (.rds)
text: benchmark evaluations executed across different computing nodes datasets different times, use combine_benchmark_results() append_benchmark_results() merge individual .rds objects single consolidated benchmark:
code: # Load two independently computed benchmark runs run1 <- readRDS("benchmark_dataset_A.rds") run2 <- readRDS("benchmark_dataset_B.rds")  # Merge into a single cross-dataset benchmark object merged_benchmark <- combine_benchmark_results(   run1, run2,   dataset_names = c("Dataset_A", "Dataset_B") )  # Compute unified cross-dataset leaderboard compute_method_leaderboard(merged_benchmark)

title: Demonstration 2: scATAC-seq Simulation Evaluation
text: Single-cell assay transposase-accessible chromatin sequencing (scATAC-seq) measures chromatin accessibility single-cell resolution. Unlike scRNA-seq expression counts, scATAC-seq data unique properties: * High Sparsity: 90% 98% values peak--cell matrices zeroes locus 2 copies per cell. * Near-Binary Nature: Values primarily represent open (accessible) vs. closed chromatin states. * Peak Co-Accessibility: Genomic loci regulated together exhibit correlated accessibility across cells. tutorial shows evaluate synthetic scATAC-seq data using scSimEval.

title: Demonstration 2: scATAC-seq Simulation Evaluation
text: scSimEval includes empirical reference simulated scATAC-seq peak accessibility dataset (example_scatac): matrices contain integer insertion counts across genomic peaks (60 peaks×80 cells60\text{ peaks} \times 80\text{ cells}).
code:
library(scSimEval)  # Load packaged scATAC-seq example data data(example_scatac)  cat("Reference scATAC-seq dimensions:", dim(example_scatac$ref), "
") #> Reference scATAC-seq dimensions: 60 80 cat("Simulated scATAC-seq dimensions:", dim(example_scatac$sim), "
") #> Simulated scATAC-seq dimensions: 60 80 cat("Cell types:", levels(example_scatac$cell_types), "
") #> Cell types: TypeA TypeB cat("Batches:", levels(example_scatac$batch_info), "
") #> Batches: Batch1 Batch2

title: Demonstration 1: scRNA-seq Simulation Evaluation
text: single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), evaluating quality simulated count data important testing analysis tools clustering, batch correction, differential expression algorithms. tutorial shows evaluate synthetic scRNA-seq data step--step using scSimEval across curated evaluation measures suite.

what: 1. Loading the Package and Example Dataset
title: Demonstration 1: scRNA-seq Simulation Evaluation
text: scSimEval includes pre-packaged real simulated scRNA-seq count matrices (example_scrna): dataset consists : * ref: Feature--cell matrix real experimental scRNA-seq read counts (60 genes ×\times 80 cells). * sim: Feature--cell matrix simulated counts generated simulation method. * cell_types: Factor cell type labels. * batch_info: Factor technical batch identifiers.

library(scSimEval)  # Load packaged scRNA-seq example data data(example_scrna)  # Examine dimensions and structure cat("Reference scRNA-seq dimensions:", dim(example_scrna$ref), "

title: Comprehensive Catalog of the 56 Evaluation Measures
text: scSimEval evaluates single-cell multiomics simulation methods using empirical reference benchmarking framework organized 56 evaluation measures across 8 canonical categories. Every measure operates directly empirical biological reference data synthetic count matrices generated simulators across scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, multiomics (scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq) layers, using normalized expressions, clustering structures, biological replicate annotations, profiling metadata.

title: Comprehensive Catalog of the 56 Evaluation Measures
text: scSimEval extracts 7 cell-level properties, 7 feature-level properties, 4 bivariate property pairs: Cell-level (7): library_size, log_library_size, tmm_factor (scRNA-seq ; omitted scATAC-seq), zero_fraction_cell, detection_freq_cell, cell_cor, pca_dist. Feature-level (7): mean_expression, variance, scaled_variance, cv, zero_fraction_feature, dispersion, gene_cor. Bivariate pairs (4): lib_vs_cellzero, mean_vs_sd, mean_vs_featzero, mean_vs_dispersion.

title: Getting Started with scSimEval: Unified Benchmarking for Single-Cell Multiomics Simulations
text: Computer simulations single-cell technologies—specifically single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), single-cell ATAC sequencing (scATAC-seq), scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq multiomics—essential bioinformatics developing pipelines, optimizing analysis workflows, evaluating statistical methods. fundamental question benchmark : realistically simulated data replicate genuine biological experiments? scSimEval provides standardized, reference-based benchmarking framework computing 56 curated evaluation measures across 8 foundational categories: Experimental reference data (ref_rna, ref_atac) Simulated synthetic data (sim_rna, sim_atac) Cell type annotations (cell_types, optional) Batch donor identifiers (batch_info, optional) Computer resources (Core-seconds memory footprint per core MiB) Developmental trajectories (automatically inferred directly count matrices) Figure 1: Unified benchmarking architecture scSimEval. end--end framework ingests reference simulated single-cell multiomics count matrices experimental metadata, evaluates 56 curated evaluation measures across eight biological computational dimensions, standardizes scores via direction-aware normalization, generates publication-grade comparative visualizations leaderboards. Supported Multiomics Modalities: scSimEval natively supports two multiomics experimental designs:4 Paired (co-assays RNA ATAC measured identical cells, e.g. 10x Multiome, SHARE-seq) full cross-modal coupling evaluation; Unpaired (independent scRNA-seq scATAC-seq separate cells tissue) unimodal evaluation plus population-level cross-modal concordance metrics. See dedicated Multiomics vignette detailed multiomics workflows.

what: 3. Score Normalization and Visual Mapping Workflow
title: Getting Started with scSimEval: Unified Benchmarking for Single-Cell Multiomics Simulations
text: single-cell benchmarking, metrics operate disparate scales directions: statistical distances near zero (lower better), runtime seconds, peak memory MiB, clustering accuracy ranges [−1,1][-1, 1] (higher better). scSimEval resolves automated two-step score normalization pipeline: Figure 2: Score normalization visual mapping workflow scSimEval. Box 1 shows two-step normalization: direction inversion lower--better metrics followed min-max scaling standard [0, 1] range. Box 2 illustrates visual mapping bubble matrices, bubble size reflects simulation quality top performers highlighted bold circular outlines. Direction Inversion: metrics smaller values indicate better simulations (e.g. KS distance, Wasserstein distance, RMSE, runtime, peak RAM), scores inverted: Inverted Value=Maximum−Value\text{Inverted Value} = \text{Maximum} - \text{Value} Min-Max Scaling (0.000.00 1.001.00): Values scaled 1.001.00 universally represents best observed performance: Standardized Score=Value−MinimumMaximum−Minimum\text{Standardized Score} = \frac{\text{Value} - \text{Minimum}}{\text{Maximum} - \text{Minimum}} bubble matrix visualizations, bubble size directly reflects standardized quality, bold circular outlines highlight top-performing simulator metric, category colors organize evaluation dimensions.

title: Getting Started with scSimEval: Unified Benchmarking for Single-Cell Multiomics Simulations
text: Install load scSimEval GitHub: scSimEval provides built-reference datasets instant testing: * example_scrna: Empirical reference simulated scRNA-seq count matrices (60 genes×80 cells60\text{ genes} \times 80\text{ cells}) cell types batch annotations. * example_scatac: Empirical reference simulated scATAC-seq peak matrices (60 peaks×80 cells60\text{ peaks} \times 80\text{ cells}). * example_rice_bud: Option B standardized Seurat v5 paired single-cell multiomics benchmark dataset rice bud tissue (100 cells, 200 genes, 200 peaks, 4 cell types, 2 batches across 6 simulators). * example_soybean_root: Option B standardized Seurat v5 unpaired single-cell multiomics benchmark dataset soybean root tissue (100 RNA cells, 100 ATAC cells, 200 genes, 200 peaks, 4 cell types, 2 batches across 3 simulators).

what: 8. Evaluating Cell Lineages and Trajectory Topology (Category VII)
title: Getting Started with scSimEval: Unified Benchmarking for Single-Cell Multiomics Simulations
text: scSimEval implements standardized dynverse trajectory evaluation workflow (Saelens et al., Nature Biotechnology, 2019) specifically within Category VII (preprocess_trajectory_hvgs() + evaluate_trajectory_metrics()). workflow models HVG transcriptomic expression dynamics, Category VII evaluated scRNA-seq automatically skipped scATAC-seq: Outlier Cell & Low-Expression QC: 3-MAD outlier cell removal library size, detected genes, mitochondrial fraction; retains genes expressed ≥5%\ge 5\% cells average expression >0.02> 0.02. HVG Selection & Zero-Convergence: Decomposes log-variance via scran::modelGeneVar (FDR < 0.05, biological variance >0.5> 0.5, adaptive fallback sparse test sets) iteratively removes -zero cells/features. Trajectory & wcor_features: Infers continuous Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) milestone graphs, evaluates , edge_flip, geodesic_correlation, F1_branches, trains ranger Random Forests (num_trees = 10000, mtry = 1% HVGs, importance = "impurity") predicting cell--milestone geodesic distances compute reference-weighted wcor_features.
code:
traj_res <- evaluate_trajectory_metrics(   ref_data = example_scrna$ref,   sim_data = example_scrna$sim,   cell_types_ref = example_scrna$cell_types,   cell_types_sim = example_scrna$cell_types,   num_trees = 500L )  cat("HIM Topology Similarity:", round(traj_res$him, 4), "
") #> HIM Topology Similarity: 1 cat("Edge Flip Similarity:", round(traj_res$edge_flip, 4), "
") #> Edge Flip Similarity: 1 cat("Geodesic Distance Correlation:", round(traj_res$geodesic_correlation, 4), "
") #> Geodesic Distance Correlation: 0.4849 cat("Branch Assignment F1:", round(traj_res$F1_branches, 4), "
") #> Branch Assignment F1: 1 cat("Dynamic Feature Importance wCor:", round(traj_res$wcor_features, 4), "
") #> Dynamic Feature Importance wCor: 0.194

text: Choose four operational modes: * Mode 1 — Pre-Computed Benchmark (Demo Data): Instantly loads complete multi-dataset evaluation across 6 simulation methods (Simulator 1 Simulator 6) 56 evaluation measures zero computational waiting time. * Mode 2 — Single-Cell Evaluation (scRNA-seq / scATAC-seq): Upload empirical reference count matrices 1–6 simulated datasets (.rds, .csv, .tsv, .txt, .xlsx). Optionally provide cell type annotations (unlocking clustering biological signal fidelity) batch labels (unlocking technical confounder mixing metrics). Set CPU worker threads parallel evaluation. * Mode 3 — Multiomics Evaluation (RNA + ATAC): Benchmark paired co-assays (e.g., 10x Multiome, SHARE-seq) unpaired multiomics datasets evaluate joint-embedding multiomics integration (batch_asw, cell_type_asw, graph_connectivity, ari, nmi) alongside per-modality unimodal properties. * Mode 4 — Upload Saved Benchmark Table (.rds / .csv): Ingest previously computed benchmark outputs evaluate_simulation_accuracy() evaluate_multiomics_accuracy(). Check “Add current benchmark results” merge multiple datasets automatically calculate cross-dataset simulator average rankings.

title: scSimEval: Unified Benchmarking for Single-Cell Multiomics Simulations
text: scSimEval unified evaluation benchmarking toolkit designed systematically quantify faithfully single-cell simulation methods reproduce empirical biological experiments. package supports: - scRNA-seq (Single-cell transcriptomic count matrices) - scATAC-seq (Single-cell chromatin accessibility peak matrices) - Paired Multiomics (Simultaneous co-assays across identical cells, e.g., 10x Multiome, SHARE-seq) - Unpaired Multiomics (Independent scRNA-seq scATAC-seq profiled separate cells biological system)

title: scSimEval: Unified Benchmarking for Single-Cell Multiomics Simulations
text: Distributional Properties (14 metrics: 10 univariate—Wasserstein, KS, MAD, MAE, RMSE, Bhattacharyya, KDE-ISE, Runs statistic, NN mismatch, Inter-dataset silhouette—4 bivariate—Fasano-Franceschini 2D KS, 2D EMD, 2D NN mismatch, 2D Inter-dataset silhouette—across 7 cell-level, 7 feature-level, 4 bivariate property pairs) Sparsity & Zero-Inflation Dynamics (5 metrics: logistic dropout midpoint/slope/R² scRNA-seq, quadratic accessibility-sparsity curve RMSE/R² scATAC-seq, posterior excess zero weight discrepancy) Cellular Manifold & Clustering Concordance (8 primary metrics: MMD, Generative Precision, Generative Recall, Silhouette ASW, Clustering Deviation Index [CDI], Neighborhood Purity, ARI, NMI, plus auxiliary Davies-Bouldin Index) Technical Variation & Batch Mixing Dynamics (5 metrics: Batch Silhouette, PCR R2R^2, CMS, Inverse Simpson Index [ISI], Cross-Batch F1) Biological Signal & Differential Fidelity (12 metrics: parallel scRNA-seq DE scATAC-seq DA suites assessing null P-value uniformity, accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC via pseudobulk edgeR-QLF) Multiomics Integration & Alignment (5 metrics: joint-embedding Batch ASW, Cell-Type ASW, Graph Connectivity, Integration ARI, Integration NMI) Trajectory & Lineage Topology (5 metrics: HVG-filtered dynverse benchmark [Saelens et al., 2019] comprising topology similarity [], edge flip similarity [edge_flip], geodesic distance correlation [geodesic_correlation], branch assignment F1 [F1_branches], Random Forest feature importance weighted correlation [wcor_features]) Computational Scalability & Efficiency (2 metrics: core-normalized execution time core-seconds [core_seconds] peak memory footprint per allocated core MiB [memory_per_core_mib], automated multi-core scaling unified memory_mb resource benchmarking) Robust Normalization Engine: Automated library-size scaling, log⁡2(CPM+1)\log_2(\text{CPM}+1) transformation, joint low-dimensional latent projections prevent technical sequencing-depth artifacts confounding evaluations. Low-Dimensional Cell Embeddings: Multi-simulator UMAP, t-SNE, PCA projections comparing reference simulated cells grid 1--1 layouts, accompanied quantitative clustering manifold quality metrics. Publication-Ready Figures & Reproducible R Scripts: Generates 600 DPI vector graphics 100% procedural, self-contained R workflow scripts (free hardcoded dput dumps) equipped dedicated file path configuration blocks local HPC cluster execution. Interactive Shiny App Studio (scSimEvalApp): Full-featured, -code graphical user interface interactive benchmark exploration, live dataset QC inspection, modality filtering, multi-format report exports.

NULL, computed via CDI::size_factor(). nfeature Integer number informative feature genes select via CDI::feature_gene_selection() (default 500L, per Fang et al., 2022). method Feature selection method passed CDI::feature_gene_selection(): "wds" (Working Dispersion Score, default) "vst". zp_threshold Numeric zero-proportion cutoff (0, 1) used pre-filter ultra-sparse features prior WDS selection (default 0.95). title: Calculate Simpipe Simulated DEG Ratio and True DEG Recovery (Approach 1) — calc_simpipe_deg_ratio
text: Evaluates ability simulation methods simulate Differentially Expressed Genes (DEGs) according Simpipe benchmarking framework (Duo et al., Genome Biology 2024). Uses edgeRQLFDetRate reference data ground truth, compares candidate DEGs returned simulation method.

title: Calculate Simpipe Simulated DEG Ratio and True DEG Recovery (Approach 1) — calc_simpipe_deg_ratio
code: calc_simpipe_deg_ratio(   ref_data,   sim_data,   ref_celltypes,   sim_celltypes,   sim_degs = NULL,   fdr_cutoff = 0.05,   logfc_cutoff = 0,   min_cells = 5 )

title: Calculate Simpipe Simulated DEG Ratio and True DEG Recovery (Approach 1) — calc_simpipe_deg_ratio
text: ref_data Reference count matrix (genes x cells). sim_data Simulated count matrix (genes x cells). ref_celltypes Factor character vector reference cell groups. sim_celltypes Factor character vector simulated cell groups. sim_degs Optional list character vectors containing candidate DEGs already returned simulation method pairwise group contrast. NULL, edgeRQLFDetRate executed sim_data detect candidate DEGs. fdr_cutoff FDR threshold true candidate DEGs (default 0.05). logfc_cutoff Absolute log2 fold change threshold (default 0). min_cells Minimum number cells per group perform DE (default 5).

title: Calculate Simpipe Simulated DEG Ratio and True DEG Recovery (Approach 1) — calc_simpipe_deg_ratio
text: list containing: P Overall weighted Simpipe true DEG recovery proportion (P) deg_ratio Overall ratio candidate/simulated DEGs true DEGs (N_given / N_true) pairwise_results Data frame per-pair details: Group1, Group2, N_true, N_given, N_overlap, P_true, DEG_ratio, Weight true_degs Named list true DEG gene vectors per pair candidate_degs Named list candidate/simulated DEG gene vectors per pair

title: Calculate Simpipe Simulated DEG Ratio and True DEG Recovery (Approach 1) — calc_simpipe_deg_ratio
text: 2 groups (\(n = 2\)): $$P = P_{\text{true}}$$ 3 groups (\(n > 2\)): $$P = \sum_{=1}^M P_{\text{true}, } \cdot \frac{N_{\text{given}, }}{N_{\text{given}}}$$ \(P_{\text{true}, }\) proportion true DEGs identified two cell groups edgeRQLFDetRate, \(N_{\text{given}, }\) denotes DEG number returned simulation method \(\)-th group pair, \(N_{\text{given}}\) denotes total DEG number across group pairs. Also calculates candidate--true DEG ratio: $$\text{DEG Ratio} = \frac{N_{\text{given}}}{N_{\text{true}}}$$

title: Master Multiomics Simulation Benchmarking Pipeline — evaluate_multiomics_accuracy
text: ref_multi Named list reference matrices Modality 1 2. sim_multi Named list simulated matrices Modality 1 2. cell_types Optional factor vector cell type labels cells. batch_info Optional factor vector batch labels cells. pairing Character string specifying whether multiomics dataset "paired" (simultaneous co-assay individual cells, e.g., 10x Chromium Multiome, SHARE-seq, SNARE-seq) "unpaired" (independent profiling modalities separate cells biological tissue). Default "paired". "unpaired" mode, cell-level pairing metrics (FOSCTTM, Match@1, cross-modal generation, direct peak--gene coupling) skipped, population-level cross-modal metrics (cross-modal label transfer, co-expression module fidelity, peak co-accessibility, accessibility profile concordance) computed alongside unimodal metrics. is_paired Optional logical alias pairing. provided, TRUE corresponds "paired" FALSE "unpaired". memory_mb Optional numeric value peak memory allocation (memory_unit). elapsed_time Optional numeric value wall-clock elapsed time (time_unit). feature_pairs Optional 2-column data.frame linked feature pairs. compute_bivariate Logical, whether compute 2D bivariate tests. Default FALSE speed. threads Number CPU threads. Default 1. verbose Logical, whether print execution progress. Default TRUE. time_unit Character string specifying unit elapsed_time: "seconds" (default, "s") "minutes" ("min"). memory_unit Character string specifying unit memory_mb: "MiB" (default, binary mebibytes) "MB" (decimal megabytes, converted MiB). sim_cores Optional positive integer specifying number CPU cores used simulator generate sim_multi. Default NULL. elapsed_time_rna, elapsed_time_atac Optional separate wall-clock runtimes RNA ATAC layers modalities simulated independently (used combined elapsed_time NULL). memory_mb_rna, memory_mb_atac Optional separate peak RAM allocations RNA ATAC layers modalities simulated independently (used combined memory_mb NULL). time_unit_rna, time_unit_atac Optional time units ("seconds" "minutes") elapsed_time_rna elapsed_time_atac; defaults time_unit. memory_unit_rna, memory_unit_atac Optional memory units ("MiB" "MB") memory_mb_rna memory_mb_atac; defaults memory_unit. sim_cores_rna, sim_cores_atac Optional positive integers specifying simulation CPU cores separate RNA ATAC runs (used combined sim_cores NULL). trajectory_num_trees Number Random Forest trees Category VII wcor_features (default 10000L, per Saelens et al. 2019).

title: Master Multiomics Simulation Benchmarking Pipeline — evaluate_multiomics_accuracy
text: Multiomics Metric Measurement Capacity Across 56 Evaluation Measures: Paired Unpaired Count Data Alone: Evaluates unimodal Category (10 univariate     + 4 bivariate metrics compute_bivariate = TRUE), Category II (5 sparsity/zero-inflation     metrics across RNA & ATAC), Category III manifold metrics (MMD, Generative Precision/Recall),     Category VII trajectory metrics inferred scRNA-seq via HVG-filtered dynverse workflow     (, edge_flip, geodesic_correlation, F1_branches, wcor_features). + Cell Types: Unlocks Category III supervised clustering concordance (Silhouette ASW,     CDI, Neighborhood Purity, ARI, NMI) Category VI (Multiomics Integration & Alignment:     Batch ASW, Cell-Type ASW, Graph Connectivity, Integration ARI, Integration NMI). + Batch / Biological Replicate Annotations: Unlocks Category IV batch mixing across     layers Category V (12 differential fidelity metrics: null P-value uniformity, accuracy,     precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC across scRNA-seq DE scATAC-seq DA). + Runtime & Memory: Logs Category VIII (core_seconds, memory_per_core_mib)     complete full 56-measure evaluation suite across 8 canonical categories.

what: Evaluate Multiomics Integration & Cross-Modal Alignment Fidelity (Category VI) — evaluate_multiomics_integration
title: Evaluate Multiomics Integration & Cross-Modal Alignment Fidelity (Category VI) — evaluate_multiomics_integration
text: Evaluates multiomics integration cross-modal alignment fidelity simulated single-cell multiomics data across 5 gold-standard integration metrics extracted key single-cell benchmarking suites (scib, scMultiSim, scCross, Matilda, scMoMtF): Batch ASW (batch_asw): Average Silhouette Width evaluating batch mixing within cell types (scib, scMultiSim). Cell-Type ASW (cell_type_asw): Average Silhouette Width evaluating cell-type bio-conservation multiomics space (scCross, scib). Graph Connectivity (graph_connectivity): Relative size largest connected component k-NN graph cell type (scCross, scMultiSim, scib). ARI (ari): Adjusted Rand Index comparing joint multiomics clustering ground-truth cell types (scib, scCross, scMultiSim, Matilda, scMoMtF). NMI (nmi): Normalized Mutual Information quantifying information concordance joint clustering cell types (scib, scCross, scMultiSim, Matilda, scMoMtF).

title: Evaluate Multiomics Integration & Cross-Modal Alignment Fidelity (Category VI) — evaluate_multiomics_integration
code: evaluate_multiomics_integration(   ref_multi = NULL,   sim_multi,   cell_types = NULL,   batch_info = NULL,   embed = NULL,   reduction_name = NULL,   n_pcs = 15,   k = 30,   threads = 1,   verbose = TRUE )

title: Evaluate Multiomics Integration & Cross-Modal Alignment Fidelity (Category VI) — evaluate_multiomics_integration
text: ref_multi Optional reference multiomics list matrices (e.g. list(rna = ..., atac = ...)). sim_multi Simulated multiomics list matrices matrix representing joint embedding coordinates. cell_types Optional cell-type vector list/data.frame annotations cell. batch_info Optional batch/donor/replicate vector list/data.frame annotations cell. embed Optional precomputed joint embedding matrix (cells x dimensions). NULL, computed automatically sim_multi. reduction_name Optional name precomputed dimensional reduction extract Seurat/SCE objects. n_pcs Number principal components per modality retain joint embedding (default 15). k Number nearest neighbors graph-based metrics (default 30). threads Number CPU threads parallel processing (default 1). verbose Logical; whether print progress messages (default TRUE).

Can provided two formats: Format (Grouped Multiomics & Unimodal): list dataset specifications, e.g.:     list("Method 1" = list(ref = list(rna = ..., atac = ...), sim = list(rna = ..., atac = ...)), "Method 3" = list(ref = ..., sim = ..., modality = "scATAC-seq")) Format B (Flat Named Datasets): list named modality datasets, e.g.:     list("Method 1-scRNA-seq" = list(ref = ..., sim = ...), "Method 1-scATAC-seq" = list(ref = ..., sim = ...), "Method 3-scATAC-seq" = list(ref = ..., sim = ...), "Method 4-scRNA-seq" = list(ref = ..., sim = ...)) pair_by_prefix Logical; TRUE (default), datasets sharing common root prefix ("Method 1-scRNA-seq" "Method 1-scATAC-seq") automatically paired multiomics joint cross-modal evaluation. what: Full Category VII Trajectory & Lineage Topology Evaluation (dynverse Workflow) — evaluate_trajectory_metrics
title: Full Category VII Trajectory & Lineage Topology Evaluation (dynverse Workflow) — evaluate_trajectory_metrics
text: Evaluates trajectory lineage preservation using standardized dynverse benchmarking framework (Saelens et al., Nature Biotechnology, 2019): Standardized cell outlier QC (3 MADs), low-expression gene filtering         (\(\ge 5\%\) cells, mean \(> 0.02\)), HVG selection (scran::modelGeneVar). Shared HVG PCA projection Docker-free Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) milestone         trajectory inference continuous cell--milestone geodesic distances. Five complementary trajectory metrics: (Hamming-Ipsen-Mikhailov similarity),         edge_flip (minimum edge flip similarity), geodesic_correlation,         F1_branches, wcor_features (ranger Random Forest feature         importance weighted correlation num_trees = 10000 1 percent mtry).

what: Real Unpaired Single-Cell Multiomics Benchmark Dataset (Soybean Root, Seurat v5 Option B) — example_soybean_root
title: Real Unpaired Single-Cell Multiomics Benchmark Dataset (Soybean Root, Seurat v5 Option B) — example_soybean_root
text: real, pre-processed unpaired single-cell RNA-seq ATAC-seq benchmark dataset soybean root tissue (Glycine max), packaged Option B (Strict S4 Standardization) using Seurat v5 objects. Contains independent empirical reference profiles (200 shared top-expressed genes x 100 RNA cells, 200 shared top-accessible peaks x 100 ATAC cells) across 4 major biological cell types (Cortex, Endodermis, Epidermis, Procambium, 25 RNA + 25 ATAC cells ) 2 biological replicates (rep1, rep2), alongside simulated outputs 3 unpaired multiomics simulators (scMultiSim, scDesign3, scCross) observed scalability benchmarks.

title: Plot Multi-Dimensional Benchmarking Bubble Matrix — plot_benchmark_bubble_matrix
text: Bubble encoding: Size: Normalized fidelity score [0, 1] – larger = better performance. Fill color: Evaluation category (one eight canonical groups). Circle (standard outline): Standard performance metric. Bold outline circle (shape 21, stroke 1.6): Top-performing simulator specific metric. Small grey dot: Metric available/computed method. Score normalization direction-aware: distance/error metrics inverted 1 always means best performance, concordance/correlation metrics used directly (higher = better).
